description: Fig. 7 is a single dual-axis line plot relating elastic-parameter trends of the Fe(1-x)Mn(x)Al system to Mn content. The x-axis is labelled "Mn content" with ticks 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0; nine square-marked data points are plotted at equal intervals from x = 0 to x = 1.0. The left y-axis is "Poisson's ratio" (range 0.22–0.34, ticks every 0.02), towards which a red arrow points; the right y-axis is "B/G" (ticks 1.5, 2.0, 2.5), towards which a blue arrow points. Two curves share the plot: red squares labelled δ (Poisson's ratio) and blue squares labelled B/G. Both curves have the same shape — a steady rise from x = 0 to a pronounced maximum at x = 0.5, a decline to a local minimum near x = 0.75, a small upturn at x = 0.875, and a steep rise to the highest value at x = 1.0. The peak at x = 0.5 reads about 0.31 on the left axis and just above the 2.2 level on the right axis; the endpoint at x = 1.0 lies near 0.325 (left) and 2.5 (right), while x = 0 is the lowest point of both curves. No numeric data labels are printed; values must be read against gridlines. The figure demonstrates that Poisson's ratio and B/G vary in parallel across the Fe–Mn–Al series, both being maximal at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al.

subfigures.description: A dual-y-axis line plot of Poisson's ratio (left axis, 0.22–0.34, red curve with red square markers, labelled δ) and B/G (right axis, 1.5–2.5, blue curve with blue square markers) versus Mn content (x-axis 0–1.0, nine equally spaced points). Both curves rise to a maximum at Mn content 0.5, dip to a local minimum near 0.75, then rise to their highest values at 1.0. Red and blue arrows mark which axis each curve refers to.

observations.observation: The plot carries two y-axes: the left one is labelled "Poisson's ratio" spanning 0.22 to 0.34, and the right one is labelled "B/G" with ticks at 1.5, 2.0 and 2.5.
The in-panel legend shows a red square labelled δ (Poisson's ratio) and a blue square labelled B/G, matching the two plotted curves.
A red arrow points leftwards from mid-plot to the Poisson's ratio axis and a blue arrow points rightwards to the B/G axis, indicating which axis each curve is read against.
Nine square-marked data points are plotted per curve between Mn content 0 and 1.0, i.e. at intervals of about 0.125.
The x-axis is labelled "Mn content" with printed ticks at 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0.
Both the δ and the B/G curves rise from their lowest values at Mn content 0 to a pronounced maximum at Mn content 0.5.
After the maximum at Mn content 0.5, both curves fall to a local minimum near Mn content 0.75 and then rise steeply to their highest values at Mn content 1.0.
At Mn content 0.5 the δ curve peaks just above the 0.30 gridline of the left axis, whereas the B/G curve peaks just above the 2.2 level of the right axis.
At Mn content 1.0 the red δ curve reaches roughly 0.325 on the left axis and the blue B/G curve reaches about 2.5 on the right axis.
No numeric value labels are printed on the data points; all values must be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states the figure shows variations in Poisson's ratio and B/G of the Fe(1-x)Mn(x)Al system.
The citing text asserts that Poisson's ratio and B/G show a similar variation trend.
The citing text asserts that the Poisson ratio reaches a maximum value for the Fe0.5Mn0.5Al alloy.
